verses.text: I made a promise with my eyes not to look with desire at a young woman.
What would God above give me? What would the Almighty in heaven give as my share?
Isn't disaster for evil people, and trouble for those who do wrong?
Doesn't God see everything I do and count every step I take?
If I have lived a lie, or my feet have hurried to cheat others,
let God weigh me on honest scales, and he will see that I have no fault.
If my steps have turned off his path, if my heart has followed what my eyes wanted, or if my hands are dirty with sin,
then let someone else eat what I have planted, and let my crops be pulled up.
If my heart has been tempted by a woman, or if I have hidden and waited at my neighbor's door,
then let my wife grind grain for another man, and let other men sleep with her.
That would be a shameful thing to do, a sin that judges should punish.
It is a fire that burns all the way to destruction. It would burn up everything I have.
If I have refused to listen to the complaints of my male or female servants when they had something against me,
what will I do when God stands up to judge me? What will I say when he asks me to explain?
Didn't the same God who made me in my mother's womb make them too? Didn't he form all of us before we were born?
If I have refused to help the poor, or let widows lose hope,
if I have kept my food to myself and not shared it with orphans,
but from the time I was young I have raised orphans as a father would, and from my birth I have guided widows;
if I have seen anyone dying for lack of clothes, or a poor person with nothing to wear,
and they did not thank me for warming them with the wool of my sheep;
if I have raised my hand against an orphan because I knew the judges at the city gate would take my side,
then let my arm fall from my shoulder, and let it be broken off at the joint.
I have always been afraid of the disaster God would send. Because of his greatness, I could not do such things.
If I have put my hope in gold, or said to pure gold, 'You are my security,'
if I have been happy because I was very rich and had gained so much,
if I have looked at the shining sun or the bright moon moving across the sky,
and my heart was secretly tempted to worship them, and I blew them a kiss with my hand,
that would also be a sin for judges to punish. I would have been unfaithful to the God who is above.
If I have been glad when my enemy was ruined, or happy when trouble came to him,
but I have never let my mouth sin by cursing his life;
if the men of my household never said, 'Who has not been fed with Job's meat?'
but no stranger ever had to spend the night in the street, because I always opened my door to travelers;
if I have hidden my sins as others do, by hiding my guilt in my heart,
because I was afraid of the crowd, or afraid of what families would think, so that I kept quiet and stayed inside;
oh, how I wish someone would listen to me! Look, I sign my name to my defense. Let the Almighty answer me! Let my accuser write down the charges against me!
I would proudly carry it on my shoulder. I would wear it like a crown.
I would tell him every step I have taken. I would come to him like a prince.
If my land cries out against me, and all its furrows are wet with tears,
if I have eaten its crops without paying, or caused the death of its owners,
then let thorns grow instead of wheat, and weeds instead of barley." This is the end of Job's words.
